_: Claude's rung of the lane ladder. A lane is an ordinal capability/price rung; a skill, an agent or a workflow stage declares a lane and NEVER a model. This file and its Codex sibling are the only two places in the repo a model name may appear, so repricing a rung or adopting a new model is a one-file change per harness. Rungs are ordered L1 (most capable) to L5 (cheapest) and mean the same thing on both harnesses -- see .agents/lanes/codex.json for the paired values and .agents/skills/lanes/SKILL.md for how a lane is chosen.

L1.summary: Irreversible work at the top of the ladder, where a mistake cannot be taken back.
L1.why: top family at the setting above `high`. For work whose mistake cannot be taken back: stored data shape, a published contract, a merge that lands.

L2.summary: Open-ended judgement at the top of the ladder, where the answer is not yet known.
L2.why: top family at its default setting. Open-ended judgement: architecture, plan authoring, a diagnosis with no known answer.

L3.summary: Ordinary specified work that a compiler or a test suite will catch.
L3.why: the workhorse. Specified work that a compiler or a test suite will catch: features, bugfixes, review lenses.

L4.summary: Mechanical work whose shape is already decided.
L4.why: the workhorse at reduced spend. Mechanical work whose shape is already decided: scripted edits, docs, ledger upkeep.

L5.summary: Clerical work with a small input and no judgement to make.
L5.why: clerical work with a small input: commit, push, pull, sync, one poll. Carries NO effort key -- Haiku 4.5 rejects `effort` outright, which is also why this rung is a capability step and not just a price step.
L5.no_effort_reason: claude-haiku-4-5 does not accept the effort parameter

frontier.summary: Frontier deliberation above the ladder, priced by provenance rather than by task shape.
frontier.why: valid only when the user explicitly asks for this tier or its model by name. Deliberately not a rung: the four lane questions grade task shape, and no answer to them may select frontier spend -- a test asserts no rung prices this model, so lane inflation can never reach it.
